heading: Filter a dict in one line
content:
A list comprehension builds a list from any iterable.
[name for name, lvl in skills.items() if lvl >= 2] keeps only the names you need.
Master lists, dicts, sets, tuples, comprehensions and f-strings first.

heading: One project, one environment
content:
Isolate each project's packages in its own virtual environment.
python -m venv .venv creates one; activate it before pip install.
Modern tools such as uv or poetry describe the project in pyproject.toml.

heading: Types and tests, the light way
An API in five lines
NumPy, pandas or Polars?
content:
NumPy: fast arrays. Vectorize instead of looping.
pandas: tabular analysis, the lingua franca of data science.
Polars: Rust-powered, multi-threaded and lazy, often much faster.

heading: Generators read big files lazily
content:
yield hands back one value at a time instead of building a whole list.
read_chunks streams a file in 1 KB pieces, so memory stays flat.
For CPU-bound work, the GIL limits threads: use processes instead.

heading: Decorators wrap behaviour
content:
A decorator takes a function and returns a wrapper around it.
The timed example prints how long each call took.
functools.wraps keeps the original name and docstring.

heading: Attention in one idea
content:
Each token creates a query, a key and a value.
Weights from softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d)) mix the values.
So every token can look at every other token, in parallel.

heading: Encoder, decoder, or both?
content:
Encoder-only (BERT): classification and embeddings.
Decoder-only (GPT, Llama): text generation.
Encoder-decoder (T5): translation and summarization.

heading: Why transformers need positions
content:
Attention on its own ignores word order.
Positional encodings such as RoPE inject where each token sits.
Without them, "dog bites man" and "man bites dog" look the same.

heading: A pretrained model in two lines
content:
pipeline("sentiment-analysis") downloads a model and wraps it for a task.
Call it on a sentence and you get a label and a score.
Find more models on the Hugging Face Hub.

heading: Fine-tune without retraining everything
content:
Full fine-tuning updates every weight, which is expensive.
LoRA and QLoRA train small adapter matrices, often on one GPU.
Try better prompts or retrieval first, and always compare against a baseline.

heading: A GPT block in 20 lines
content:
Causal self-attention, then an MLP, each with LayerNorm and a residual connection.
is_causal=True stops tokens from seeing the future.
Stack N blocks, add embeddings and a vocabulary layer: that is a GPT.

heading: Why generation needs a KV cache
content:
Each new token attends to every earlier token.
The KV cache keeps their keys and values instead of recomputing them.
It is one of the key techniques for serving large models.

heading: Quantization: smaller weights
content:
8-bit or 4-bit weights cut memory 2-4x.
Formats include GPTQ, AWQ and GGUF.
The lesson loads a 7B model in 4-bit with load_in_4bit=True.

heading: What an LLM actually learns
content:
LLMs are decoder-only transformers trained to predict the next token.
Instruction tuning and RLHF then teach them to follow requests.
Know the terms: tokens, context window, temperature, hallucination.

heading: A four-point prompt checklist
content:
Give a clear role, task and output format.
Add a few examples.
Ask for JSON and validate it.
Keep instructions apart from untrusted input.

heading: RAG in four steps
content:
Split documents into chunks.
Embed and store them in a vector database.
Retrieve the top-k chunks for a question, then generate with them.
Measure retrieval separately from answers.

heading: Agents need guardrails
content:
An agent lets an LLM call tools in a loop.
In production add output validation, cost limits and tracing.
Run evaluation sets in CI so changes don't quietly regress.

heading: Why chunks overlap
content:
Chunks of 800 characters with 100 of overlap.
A sentence cut at a boundary still appears whole in one chunk.
Retrieval then has a fair chance of finding it.

heading: Teach the bot to say "I don't know"
content:
Tell the model to answer using only the retrieved context.
If the answer is not there, it should say so.
That one line reduces made-up answers.

heading: How tool calling works
content:
You describe a function with a JSON schema.
The model returns a structured call; your code runs it.
The result goes back to the model. Cap the loop and validate arguments.

heading: MCP: one integration, many assistants
content:
The Model Context Protocol exposes tools, resources and prompts through an MCP server.
Any MCP client can then use them.
Treat tool output as untrusted input.

heading: Evals belong in CI
content:
Build a golden dataset of inputs with expected properties.
Score with exact checks, similarity or an LLM-as-judge rubric.
Run it whenever a prompt or model changes.

heading: Similar meaning, nearby vectors
content:
An embedding maps text, images or audio to a vector.
"deploy a container" lands near "run a docker image", far from "bake a cake".
Cosine similarity is the usual measure for text.

heading: Trade a little recall for speed
content:
Exact search compares every vector: too slow at millions of rows.
HNSW builds a layered graph: high recall, more memory.
Always measure recall@k against exact search.

heading: Already on Postgres? Start with pgvector
content:
pgvector keeps vectors next to your relational data.
Dedicated stores like Qdrant or Pinecone scale to billions.
Compare filtering, hybrid search, multi-tenancy and cost.

heading: Keywords plus vectors
content:
Vectors miss exact terms like error codes; keywords miss synonyms.
Reciprocal Rank Fusion merges both ranked lists.
A cross-encoder re-ranker on the top 50 sharpens precision.

heading: Most models die after the notebook
content:
MLOps brings DevOps discipline to models.
Version data, track experiments, register approved models.
Automate training, serve, and monitor for drift.

heading: Data drift vs concept drift
content:
Data drift: the inputs change.
Concept drift: the link between inputs and labels changes.
Retrain when drift crosses a threshold, and promote only if the new model beats the champion.
